newsitem.title: ITALY: Cracks appear in Italy's opposition bloc.
newsitem.headline: Cracks appear in Italy's opposition bloc.

text.p: Italian hard-right leader Gianfranco Fini met former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi on Friday to discuss growing strains in their opposition alliance.
Fini and Berlusconi held more than two hours of talks on the future of the bloc, the centre-right Freedom Alliance, after differences this week over policy brought tensions to the fore.

"We began our view and we agreed that it is indispensable to save the Freedom Alliance," Fini told reporters. "Personally I believe that there is still a lot to clear up before that objective is reached," he added.

Berlusconi, who leads the opposition bloc, has been at odds with Fini over how much cooperation to offer Italy's governing centre-left coalition on two key issues, constitutional reform and economic policy.

Berlusconi's conservative Forza Italia party supported the election on Wednesday of the leader of the main government party, Massimo D'Alema of the Democratic Party of the Left, as chairman of a parliamentary commission on constitutional change.
Fini's National Alliance abstained in the vote.

Strains have also arisen over a statement by Berlusconi this week declaring readiness to discuss a government proposal to bring forward passage of next year's budget as long as the measures include cuts to spending on pensions and health.
Both developments have prompted political speculation that D'Alema and Berlusconi, whose two parties are the biggest in Italy, may be jockeying to form a "grand coalition".
"We remain firm and decisive in our opposition to the government. We have no desire to become part of the government majority," Berlusconi said after his talks with Fini.
He said the two politicians had agreed to meet again "to outline our strategy for the next four years".

The strains between Berlusconi and Fini have also caused waves for the government, which depends for its survival in the lower house of parliament on external support from the hard left party Communist Refoundation.

Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti said on Thursday that it would bring down the government if it cut pensions and urged Prime Minister Romano Prodi to reject what he called Berlusconi's "mortal embrace".
